notes: Conservative, sourced dataset of Stockholm tech-ecosystem organisations for the Founder Map layer. All lat/lon are null by design; coordinates are geocoded later from OpenStreetMap (ODbL, '© OpenStreetMap contributors'). Addresses are recorded only where a cited source states them; aggregator-sourced addresses are flagged in each entry's notes. District values derived from an address/postcode are inferences to be confirmed by geocoding; district-precision entries are placed at district anchors and labelled approximate in-game. 'other' district = outside the listed districts or unknown (check precision). Fields set to null mean 'not verified', not 'false'. Founder names are public historical facts only: the game must not portray real people as characters, and storyline_hooks are challenge archetypes for fictional missions with no implied endorsement. Status facts reflect sources seen up to 2026-11-23 and will go stale. Wikipedia was rate-limited during research, so some Wikipedia citations were seen via search-result extracts rather than full pages.

entries.name: Spotify
entries.summary: Music streaming service founded in Stockholm in April 2006. It went public on 3 April 2018 through a direct listing on the New York Stock Exchange, without raising new capital. Wikipedia reports over 788 million monthly active users (306 million paying subscribers) as of March 2026. Since 1 January 2026 Daniel Ek has been executive chairman, with Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström serving as co-CEOs.

status.label: public
status.detail: Listed on NYSE since the April 2018 direct listing. Spotify AB is headquartered in Stockholm.

unicorn.note: Was a private unicorn before 2018; publicly listed since April 2018.

storyline_hooks: Licensing gauntlet: get rights holders to sign before the launch window closes.
Freemium economics: convert free users to paying ones without driving the free users away.
Leadership handover: a founder moves up to chairman and the team must keep shipping.

sources.title: Harvard Law School Forum: Spotify direct listing case study
NPR: Daniel Ek to step aside as CEO (2025-09-30)

entries.notes: The listed entity is Spotify Technology S.A. (Luxembourg). Wikipedia describes the listing as American depositary receipts; it is recorded here only as 'NYSE: SPOT'. The office is in the 'Urban Escape' block, per the Spotify newsroom.

entries.name: Klarna
entries.summary: Payments and 'buy now, pay later' company founded in Stockholm in 2005 (originally Kreditor Europe AB) after its founders took part in the Stockholm School of Economics entrepreneurship competition. It created a UK holding company (Klarna Group plc, incorporated in England and Wales) in 2023–24, ahead of an IPO. Klarna listed on the NYSE on 10 September 2025 at $40 per share (about $15B valuation). The share price later fell well below the IPO price. Q3 2026 revenue was about $1.01B, with a net loss of $65M.

status.label: public
status.detail: NYSE-listed since September 2025 through Klarna Group plc (England and Wales). The operating bank, Klarna Bank AB (publ), keeps its registered head office in Stockholm.

unicorn.note: Was one of Europe's most valuable private fintechs before the IPO; public since September 2025.

locations.label: Klarna Bank AB registered and head office

storyline_hooks: Trust problem: persuade shoppers and merchants that a new checkout is safe.
Credit-loss squeeze: grow lending volume without letting defaults eat the margin.
Going public: restructure the holding company and survive the share price after the IPO.

sources.title: Fortune: Klarna jumps in NYSE debut (2025-09-11)
CNBC: Klarna sets up UK holding company (2023-11-06)
The Next Web: Klarna Q3 2026 results

entries.notes: Some finance sites list Klarna as 'based in London' because of the UK plc. The Stockholm address is the head office of Klarna Bank AB. Share-price figures move constantly and are deliberately left out of the summary.

entries.name: King (Candy Crush)
entries.summary: Mobile and social game maker founded in Stockholm in August 2003 as Midasplayer.com and renamed King.com in 2005. It rose to fame with Candy Crush Saga (2012). Activision Blizzard bought it for $5.9B, closing in February 2016. Microsoft completed its purchase of Activision Blizzard on 13 October 2023, so King is now part of Microsoft's Xbox. In July 2025 it cut about 10% of its staff (around 200 jobs), mostly in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Part of Microsoft (Xbox), via Activision Blizzard. Wikipedia: headquartered in Stockholm and London, incorporated in Malta.

unicorn.note: Went public in 2014 at a valuation of around $7B. No longer independent.

storyline_hooks: Near-bankruptcy: keep a browser-game startup alive until a hit arrives.
One-hit risk: follow up a mega-hit casual game.
Corporate parent: keep a studio's culture after two acquisitions in a row.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Activision Blizzard closes $5.9B acquisition of King (2016-02-23)
Microsoft blog: welcoming Activision Blizzard King (2023-10-13)

entries.notes: The Sveavägen 44 address comes from 2015 architecture coverage. Whether King is still there in 2026 is unconfirmed, so it is marked historical. The founder list follows the Wikipedia infobox as reported in search results; other sources omit some names.

entries.name: Mojang Studios (Minecraft)
entries.summary: Game studio founded in Stockholm in 2009 by Markus Persson around Minecraft. Mojang AB was incorporated in 2010. Microsoft announced the purchase on 15 September 2014 for $2.5B and completed it on 6 November 2014. Today Mojang Studios is an Xbox studio based in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary

unicorn.note: Acquired for $2.5B in 2014; not independent since.

entries.name: Skype
entries.founded_in: Registered in Luxembourg; software developed in Tallinn (Swedish and Danish founders)
entries.summary: Internet calling service founded in 2003 by Swede Niklas Zennström and Dane Janus Friis. The software was written by Estonian engineers (Ahti Heinla, Priit Kasesalu and Jaan Tallinn). The company was registered in Luxembourg and had offices including Tallinn and Stockholm. Microsoft completed its $8.5B acquisition on 13 October 2011. Microsoft retired the consumer Skype service on 5 May 2025 and moved users to Teams Free.

status.label: defunct
status.detail: Consumer service retired by Microsoft on 5 May 2025. Users were migrated to Microsoft Teams Free.

unicorn.note: Acquired by Microsoft for $8.5B in 2011; the service no longer runs.

Legacy sunset: migrate millions of users when a parent company retires a product.

No Stockholm street address was found. district is 'other' (unknown). Present it in-game as a historical landmark, not a current company.

entries.name: Zettle by PayPal (formerly iZettle)
entries.summary: Mobile card-reader and point-of-sale company founded in Stockholm in April 2010. It launched its first app and chip-card reader in 2011. PayPal agreed to buy iZettle in May 2018, cancelling a planned IPO, and completed the roughly $2.2B deal on 20 September 2018. The company renamed itself 'Zettle by PayPal' in February 2021.

unicorn.note: Acquired for about $2.2B in 2018 (PayPal's largest deal at the time).

entries.name: Tink
entries.summary: Open-banking platform founded in Stockholm in 2012. It connects to more than 3,400 banks across Europe. Visa announced the deal in June 2021 (about €1.8B) and completed it on 10 March 2022; Visa's filings report about $1.9B in cash. Tink runs as a standalone Visa subsidiary, and Visa said its headquarters would stay in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Wholly owned subsidiary of Visa since March 2022.

unicorn.note: Acquired by Visa in 2022 for about €1.8B.

storyline_hooks: Bank integrations: connect to thousands of banks, each with its own quirks.
Regulatory clock: build a product around a new open-banking rule.

entries.name: Lovable
entries.summary: AI app-building ('vibe coding') company founded in Stockholm in 2023, growing out of the open-source GPT Engineer project. Its rounds: a $15M pre-Series A led by Creandum (February 2025); a $200M Series A at a $1.8B valuation led by Accel (July 2025); a $330M Series B at $6.6B (December 2025); and a $400M Series C at $13.3B led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund (12 August 2026). Antler was its first investor. The company says Stockholm remains its centre of gravity.

status.label: private
status.detail: Venture-backed. Valued at $13.3B in the August 2026 Series C.

unicorn.note: Became a unicorn in July 2025 (Series A at $1.8B). Latest round: $13.3B (Aug 2026).

storyline_hooks: Hypergrowth: hire and scale infrastructure fast enough to keep up with sign-ups.
Open source to company: turn a viral GitHub project into a product people pay for.
Talent magnet: keep the HQ in Stockholm while opening offices abroad.

A directory site (komo.ai) gives 'Regeringsgatan 25', but this is unconfirmed and not recorded. Fabian Hedin previously worked at Depict.ai.

entries.name: Legora (formerly Leya)
entries.summary: Legal AI platform founded in Stockholm in 2023 as Leya. It went through Y Combinator (Winter 2024) and renamed itself Legora in February 2025. Its rounds: an $80M Series B at $675M (May 2025); a $150M Series C at $1.8B led by Bessemer (30 October 2025); a $550M Series D at $5.55B (March 2026, later extended to $600M); and a $550M Series E at $8.8B post-money led by Atreides (October 2026). It opened a New York office in 2025 and has expanded across the US.

status.label: private
status.detail: Venture-backed. Valued at $8.8B post-money in the October 2026 Series E.

unicorn.note: Became a unicorn with the October 2025 Series C ($1.8B). Latest round: $8.8B (Oct 2026).

locations.label: Legora (origin and HQ listed in company profiles)

Head-to-head rival: race a better-funded US competitor for the same firms.

entries.name: Epidemic Sound
entries.summary: Royalty-free soundtrack music platform for creators, founded in Stockholm in 2009. In March 2021 it raised $450M at a $1.4B valuation from EQT Growth and Blackstone Growth. In 2026 it announced a move beyond its music catalogue toward a broader creative platform. The parent company is being renamed Epidemic Group AB. Co-founder Oscar Höglund stepped down as CEO; CFO Sara Börsvik is interim CEO. The company reported a return to profitable growth in 2026.

entries.name: Truecaller
entries.summary: Caller ID and spam-blocking app founded in Stockholm in 2009 by two KTH computer-science graduates. It listed on Nasdaq Stockholm on 8 October 2021 at SEK 52 per Class B share (ticker TRUE B), valuing it at roughly $2.2B. Most users and many employees are in India. Its Q3 2026 report (November 2026) described a 'return to growth following a successful strategic reset' under CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala.

entries.name: Northvolt
entries.summary: Battery maker founded in Stockholm (as SGF Energy) by two former Tesla executives. It built the Northvolt Ett gigafactory in Skellefteå in northern Sweden. Northvolt filed for bankruptcy in Sweden in March 2025 and stopped production in June 2025. US battery company Lyten agreed to buy its remaining assets in Sweden (Northvolt Ett, Northvolt Labs in Västerås) and Germany (Northvolt Drei) and has begun restarting operations.

entries.summary: Shared e-scooter and e-bike operator founded in Stockholm in 2018, operating in more than 110 European cities. A $115M Series D in December 2021 valued it at just over $1B. Voi reported its first profitable year in 2024 and record results in 2025. Its CFO has said an IPO is a 'natural long-term option' but there are 'no concrete plans'.

status.detail: Venture arm of EQT AB.

storyline_hooks: Data-driven VC: get your fictional startup noticed by an investor's deal-sourcing algorithm.
entries.notes: The address comes from an aggregator, and CB Insights gives 2015 as the founding year (Wikipedia says 2016). status.label is 'subsidiary' because it is part of the EQT group; acquired_by names the parent, not an acquisition.

entries.name: Northzone
entries.summary: Venture capital firm founded in 1996, originally in Oslo, with offices including Stockholm, London, New York, Berlin and Amsterdam. Partner Pär-Jörgen Pärson led its 2008 investment in Spotify's Series A. It closed a $500M fund in 2019. Other earlier bets include iZettle and Trustpilot.

status.label: private
status.detail: Operating VC firm.

storyline_hooks: Board seat: manage an investor who wants a say in your strategy.

sources.title: Northzone: Spotify, the impossible success story

entries.notes: One article places the office on the 16th floor; the official page says 15th. Founded in Oslo, not Stockholm.

entries.name: Kista Science City
entries.summary: Innovation district in Kista, north-west Stockholm, often described as Europe's largest ICT cluster. Ericsson moved production there from 1975 and its HQ in 2003. Industry, academia and the City of Stockholm formed the Electrum Foundation in 1986, and the shared 'science city' vision dates from 1999. Kista Science City AB is a non-profit wholly owned by the Electrum Foundation. Ericsson announced in 2026 that it plans to leave Kista for Hagastaden from around 2028.

status.label: nonprofit
status.detail: Cluster organisation (Kista Science City AB) owned by the Electrum Foundation.

storyline_hooks: Suburban tech hub: weigh cheaper Kista space against being near city-centre investors.
Anchor tenant leaving: the district's biggest employer announces a move.

sources.title: Nordregio: Kista wants entrepreneurial ICT students

entries.notes: founded_year = 1986 (Electrum Foundation); one weaker source says 1985. 'Europe's largest ICT cluster' is a common claim but not independently measured here.

entries.name: Stockholm School of Economics (SSE)
entries.summary: Private business school founded by Swedish business leaders. It opened in 1909 at Brunkebergstorg and moved in 1926 to Sveavägen 65, still its main building. Klarna's founders met through its entrepreneurship competition. Its incubator, SSE Business Lab, is listed separately.

status.label: institution
status.detail: Private university-level business school.

storyline_hooks: Business plan competition: enter a student contest that could launch a company.
entries.notes: District (Vasastan) is inferred from the address; confirm with OSM. The SSE timeline says the association behind the school formed in 1906.

entries.name: SSE Business Lab
entries.summary: Startup incubator of the Stockholm School of Economics, launched in 2001 and open to SSE students, alumni and faculty. SSE says it has supported more than 350 companies, including Klarna, Voi, Legora, Budbee and Quinyx. It is housed in SSE's 'House of Innovation'.

status.label: institution
status.detail: University incubator, operating.

storyline_hooks: Alumni network: use an incubator's network to land your first enterprise customer.
entries.notes: The exact building and address of the 'House of Innovation' were not confirmed, so the location is at district precision, assumed to be near the SSE main campus. Company counts differ between pages (250+ vs 350+).

entries.name: SUP46 (Start-Up People of Sweden)
entries.summary: Startup hub and coworking community launched in October 2013 on Regeringsgatan in central Stockholm. Its official opening press release credits Spotify's Daniel Ek with opening it. Realtid reported in July 2026 that it hosts about 60 startups, with co-founder Jessica Stark as CEO.

status.label: private
status.detail: Operating startup hub.

storyline_hooks: Community hub: build a reputation through events and peer introductions.
entries.notes: The Regeringsgatan 65 vs 29 history comes from search snippets; confirm on the Visit Stockholm page before final placement. CB Insights lists Tegelbacken 4A (likely outdated).

entries.name: Almi Invest
entries.summary: State-owned early-stage venture investor (part of Almi AB, ultimately owned by the Swedish state), launched in 2009. It invests pre-seed to early Series A in Swedish companies, always alongside private co-investors, typically taking 10–15% in the first round. It runs eight regional funds plus a national GreenTech vehicle.

status.label: institution
status.detail: State-owned venture investor.

storyline_hooks: Matched funding: find a private co-investor so the public fund can join your round.

sources.title: Almi: about Almi Invest and our mission
OECD: benchmarking government support for VC (Sweden)

entries.notes: Almi's 'most active investor' claim is self-reported. No Stockholm office address was recorded.

entries.name: Industrifonden
entries.summary: Evergreen venture capital foundation set up by the Swedish government in 1979, headquartered in Stockholm. It has invested in small and medium-sized companies since 1996 and now focuses on Nordic deep tech, life science and transformative tech. It reinvests returns rather than distributing them.

status.label: institution
status.detail: Independent evergreen foundation.

storyline_hooks: Deep-tech round: convince a patient investor that your hardware science can scale.

sources.title: OECD: benchmarking government support for VC (Sweden)

entries.notes: Fund-size figures differ between sources (SEK 4–5B), so they are left out.

entries.name: Antler (Stockholm / Nordics)
entries.summary: Global early-stage investor and founder residency programme. Stockholm was its first office outside Singapore, where Antler started, and is the base for its Nordic residency (other Nordic offices: Oslo 2020, Copenhagen 2022, Helsinki 2024). Antler was Lovable's first investor and returned for Lovable's August 2026 Series C.

status.label: private
status.detail: Operating early-stage investor.

storyline_hooks: Co-founder matching: join a residency alone and leave with a team and a pre-seed cheque.

sources.title: Antler: Lovable Series C press release

entries.notes: Antler's founding year was not cleanly confirmed (search summaries were ambiguous), so it is left null. Programme length differs between pages (8 or 10 weeks).

entries.name: Nordic Tech Week
entries.summary: City-wide tech festival held in Stockholm every September, modelled on decentralised 'tech week' formats, with 300+ independently hosted events (panels, hackathons, investor gatherings). The 2026 edition ran 7–11 September 2026 and included a Startup Day and the open-air Tech Open at Kungsträdgården.

status.label: private
status.detail: Recurring annual event (September).

storyline_hooks: Tech week sprint: a week of side events and chance meetings that can make or break a fundraise.

sources.title: KTH: KTH Innovation Collide at Nordic Tech Week

entries.notes: The organiser and first edition year were not confirmed. Kungsträdgården is placed in Norrmalm (district inferred). Attendance figures (around 25,000) come from a source not used here.

entries.name: STHLM Tech Fest / SthlmTech meetup (historical)
entries.summary: Community-run Stockholm startup festival that grew out of the SthlmTech group's monthly meetups, organised from 2013. The 2014 edition at the Stockholm Waterfront drew about 3,000 attendees, 100 startups and 50+ investor groups. In 2019 it expanded into the first STHLM Tech Week.

status.label: defunct
status.detail: Current status unknown. No 2026 edition under this name was found.

storyline_hooks: Meetup to festival: grow a monthly community meetup into a city-wide event.

sources.title: The Local: Stockholm Tech Fest live blog (2014)
Nordic Startup News: 3000 Tech Fest attendees

entries.notes: status.label 'defunct' means 'not confirmed active'. Treat it as historical inspiration only. The link between STHLM Tech Week (2019) and Nordic Tech Week was not established.
